Clash Manager database atlas

This is a map of what the database stores, how the pieces connect, and where measured costs deserve investigation. Select an object to inspect its purpose, lifecycle and dependencies. The inventory reads metadata and aggregate counts; it does not modify the database.

How data reaches the app

Clash Royale API → Edge Functions → raw responses → normalization triggers → players, members, recruits and battles → feature views and RPCs → PWA and Android app.

A table stores rows. An index stores an additional lookup structure that speeds reads but costs storage and writes. A view computes a result when read. A trigger automatically runs extra work when data changes. A routine / RPC is database code. A scheduled job launches recurring work; launching a function does not prove it completed.

Overflow storage (TOAST) holds large values such as JSON payloads. Its physical size includes reusable space, so it cannot be equated with reclaimable waste. Row and usage estimates can reset or lag behind actual data.

      Audit coverage and limits
          A captured inventory is not a claim that every query, access rule or recovery path has been verified. Regenerate with pnpm db:audit --output /path/report; compare using --compare older.snapshot.json. Use pnpm db:health for current connectivity, freshness and host evidence.
